title: Mediterranean Chickpea Bowls
subtitle: Plant-forward without feeling light
description: Mediterranean Chickpea Bowls is a mediterranean bowl built for a hungry firehall crew — Plant-forward without feeling light. Hearty portions, station-kitchen timing, and flavors everyone recognizes after a long shift.
equipment: Large cast iron skillet or Dutch oven

ingredients.name: Primary protein or hearty veg base

steps.title: Prep the line
steps.instruction: Set out all ingredients for Mediterranean Chickpea Bowls before you turn on heat — firefighters eat on a schedule. Pat proteins dry and season aggressively with salt and pepper; dry surfaces brown instead of steam.

steps.title: Build the base
steps.instruction: Heat oil in your largest skillet, Dutch oven, or on the flat-top over medium-high until it shimmers. Add aromatics (onion first) and cook until the edges turn golden and the smell sweetens — usually 4–6 minutes. If garlic is in the recipe, add it after the onion softens so it doesn't burn.

steps.title: Cook the main
steps.instruction: Cook the primary protein or base for Mediterranean Chickpea Bowls until it hits proper color and safe internal temperature. Don't crowd the pan — work in batches if needed so you get browning, not gray stew. Listen for a steady sizzle; if it's silent, the heat is too low.

steps.title: Finish and season
steps.instruction: Bring components together, taste, and adjust salt. Sauce should coat, not pool. If cheese is involved, melt it just until glossy — another 1–2 minutes under a lid or broiler. Let heavy proteins rest 5 minutes before slicing.

steps.title: Serve the hall
steps.instruction: Transfer to sheet trays or a serving line immediately. Keep backup warm at 200°F. Call the crew while it's hot — this meal is built for a hungry hall, not a photo shoot.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold protein after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
tonightSpread: Build bowls base → grain → protein → toppings so the line moves in one direction.
Put hot components closest to the crew, cold crunch at the far end.
Portion bowls on the line with protein visible on top — crew eats with their eyes first.
Keep dressing and crunchy toppings in side bowls so greens stay crisp through second servings.
Line up Mediterranean Chickpea Bowls on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
